subject.title: [Security] Session hijacking vulnerability due to predictable sequence IDs in gateway client

question: Does gateway security ownership confirm that predictable event-order sequence numbers are non-authoritative and non-exploitable, or can the reporter provide a concrete cross-connection injection path that warrants private advisory handling?
rationale: Protected security labels require explicit human disposition, and only a security owner should formally conclude that the report does not cross an authentication or transport-integrity boundary.

options.title: Confirm non-vulnerability
options.body: Confirm that event sequence metadata grants no authority and close unless a concrete credential-free or cross-connection exploit is supplied.

options.title: Request a minimal PoC
options.body: Ask for exact frames, attacker prerequisites, authentication state, transport position, and the accepted unauthorized operation before deciding.

options.title: Escalate privately
options.body: Move the report to private advisory handling if maintainers can reproduce message acceptance across an authentication, authorization, or connection boundary.

recommendation.title: Confirm non-vulnerability
recommendation.body: Confirm that event sequence metadata grants no authority and close unless a concrete credential-free or cross-connection exploit is supplied.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history shows the strongest concentration of gateway authentication and security-boundary hardening work.
